about.title: Santee Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Santee residents rely on a handful of nearby clinics, urgent care centers, and San Diego County hospitals for everything from routine checkups to emergency care after a crash on Mission Gorge Road or SR-52. Most of the time, that care goes fine. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mismanaged, the harm can be lasting. Medical malpractice claims in California are different from ordinary injury cases — they involve stricter deadlines, a required pre-suit notice, and rules about expert review that most people have never encountered before. We handle medical malpractice cases and can review your medical records, explain whether the case appears to meet California's legal standards, and walk through next steps in plain language.

items.title: Deadlines Are Short and Strict
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement — waiting to sort out records can cost you the claim.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically has to confirm the care fell below the accepted standard; a poor outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice, so early case evaluation matters.

items.title: Damages Rules Are Complex
items.desc: California's cap on non-economic damages rises each year under MICRA, and how a claim is valued depends on details our team is positioned to walk through with you.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Santee?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from when it happened. There's also a 90-day notice you must give before filing suit. Because these deadlines can overlap in confusing ways, it helps to have us review your specific timeline early.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No — California law requires proof that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, usually backed by a qualified expert. A treatment that simply didn't work as hoped isn't enough on its own. We can help determine whether your situation involves an actual departure from standard care.

items.question: Do you handle malpractice claims tied to Santee hospitals directly?
items.answer: Yes — we handle medical malpractice claims in San Diego County. If you were treated at a facility serving the Santee area, we can review your case and advise on the specific medical provider involved.
